text:
alex: hey all — alex here, day 2 on runtime. Trying to build from source on dl-build-03 (ubuntu20.04). Build completes but `run_tests` segfaults immediately. Can someone point me to infra owners or quick fixes?

alex: build steps I used:
```
mkdir build && cd build
CC=gcc-9 CXX=g++-9 cmake .. -DREDWOOD_USE_CUDA=ON -DCUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR=/usr/local/cuda-11.8
make -j16
ctest -j1 -R run_tests --output-on-failure
```

alex: failing snippet from the test run:
```
[ RUN      ] gpu_inference.simple_forward
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  CUDA kernel launch failure: invalid configuration argument
Aborted (core dumped)
```

alex: I saw mixed libcudnn/libcuda versions in the container. Not sure if that's it. Also have only user-level access on that host.

sara: hey alex — welcome! :wave: first quick things: (1) confirm `nvidia-smi` and `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version` on the host, (2) check ldd of the binary to see which libcuda/cu* are being picked up.

sara: try:
```
ssh dl-build-03
nvidia-smi
ldd build/bin/runtime_tests | grep -E "cuda|cudnn|cublas|cusparse"
```

matt: tagging infra — @matt: that host sometimes has a stale system driver from the AMI and people mount a newer container libcuda which causes JIT/ptx errors. If you can't run `nvidia-smi` let me know and I can give you sudo access to check modules.

ops-bot: CI alert: recent push to branch feature/runtime-refactor triggered flaky_gpu_test failure on dl-build-03 at 2056789005. Link: https://ci.internal/redwood/12345 (log snippet attached).

alex: ran ldd, here's the relevant lines:
```
libcudart.so.11 => /usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64/libcudart.so.11 (0x00007f...)
libcublas.so.11 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublas.so.11 (0x00007f...)
libcudnn.so.8 => /opt/cudnn/8.2/lib64/libcudnn.so.8 (0x00007f...)
libcuda.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (0x00007f...)
```

alex: so libcudnn 8.2 vs toolkit 11.8 — any incompatibility there?

sara: that mismatch could definitely bite. Also the "invalid configuration argument" often means PTX compiled for a higher compute capability than the driver supports or the JIT can't compile because of driver-toolkit mismatch. Two quick options: (A) run inside our recommended docker image `redwood/dev-runtime:cuda11.8-gcc9` (it pins cudnn/driver libs), or (B) force the binary to use the host's libcuda by unsetting container LD_LIBRARY_PATH before running tests: `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH ctest ...`

matt: if you want, I can spin up a fresh dev VM with the approved AMI and give you creds. ping me here and I'll provision (takes ~10m).

sara: one more tip: set `REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DEBUG_PTXXX=1` to get the kernel ptx dump in logs, helps us see if it's an unsupported arch.

alex: pulled image and re-ran inside container, same error but logs now show JIT fallback message: `ptxas fatal   : Unsupported .version 7.5`

alex: looks like PTX version is too new for the host driver — what driver version do we need?

matt: driver 525+ generally supports 7.5 PTX? but depends on GPU. Run `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,name --format=csv` on host. If host driver < 520 we should upgrade. I'll check dl-build-03 and update if safe.

sara: short-term workaround: build with lower arch/PTX by adding `-DCUDA_NVCC_FLAGS="-arch=sm_80 -gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80"` (match your card) or `-gencode=arch=compute_70,code=sm_70` to force older PTX. Longer-term we'll standardize the base images.

alex: great — lowered arch to sm_70 and tests pass locally in container. Will open a ticket to request driver upgrade for dl-build-03. Thanks everyone! :tada:

matt: :thumbsup: filing infra ticket now (INFRA-789) and will coordinate maintenance window.

sara: welcome to the runtime team! shout if you hit more weirdness — most first-week issues are driver/lib mismatches.
